spans.s:
अष्टन् अष्टन्, अ or औ (but अष्टौ is more
common for nom., acc., and voc. cases), pl. eight
[cf. Lat. octo; Gr. ὀκτώ Goth. ahtau; Mod. Germ.
acht; Eng. eight; Lith. aszt˚uni; Slav. osmj]; in
comp. with other numerals often अष्टा, e. g. अष्टा-
दशन्, eighteen; अष्टादश, अस्, ई, अम्, the eigh-
teenth, divided into eighteen parts; अष्टादश-धा,
eighteen-fold; अष्टा-विंशति, twenty-eight; अष्टा-
विंश, अस्, ई, अम्, the twenty-eighth, divided in-
to twenty-eight parts; अष्टात्रिंश, अस्, ई, अम्,
the thirty-eighth, containing thirty-eight; अष्टा-
चत्वारिंश, अस्, ई, अम्, the forty-eighth.
—अष्ट-
कर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has the number eight
as a mark burnt in his ear; (अस्), m. eight-eared,
an epithet of Brahmā, who is supposed to have four
heads; (ई), m., N. of a man.
—अष्ट-कृत्वस्, ind.
eight times.
—अष्ट-कोण, अस्, m. an octagon.
—अष्ट-खण्ड, अस्, m. title of a collection of
several sections of the Ṛg-veda.
—अष्ट-गव, अम्,
n. a flock of eight cows.
—अष्ट-गाध् (?), त्, m. a
fabulous animal (called Śarabha), supposed to have
eight legs; a spider (?).
—अष्ट-गुण, अस्, आ, अम्,
eight-fold; (अम्), n. the eight qualities.
—अष्ट-
गुणाश्रय (˚ण-आश्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, endowed with the
eight qualities, epithet of a king.
—अष्ट-त्व, अम्,
n. condition of eight.
—अष्ट-दंष्ट्र, अस्, m.,
N. of a son of Virūpa, author of a hymn of the
Ṛg-veda; N. of a Dānava.
—अष्ट-दल, an octa-
gon.
—अष्ट-दिक्-पाल, आस्, m. pl. the regents of
the cardinal points, as Indra of the East, Agni or
Vahni of the S. E., Yama of the South, Nairṛta of
the S. W., Varuṇa of the West, Marut of the N. W.,
[]
Kuvera of the North, and Īśa or Śiva of the N. E.
—अष्ट-दिश्, क्, f. the eight cardinal points of the
compass collectively.
—अष्ट-धा, ind. eight-fold,
eight times, in eight parts or sections.
—अष्ट-
धातु, उ, n. the eight metals collectively, as gold,
silver, copper, tin, lead, brass, iron, and steel.
—अष्ट-
पद, अस्, m. a Vedic metre of eight Padas.
—अष्ट-
पाद्, त्, त्, त्, having eight legs; (त्), m. a spider;
a fabulous animal with eight legs.
—अष्ट-पाद, अस्,
आ, अम्, having eight legs; (अस्), m. a kind of spider
with a small body and long legs.
—अष्ट-पादिका,
f., N. of the plant Vallaris Dichotomus Wall.
—अष्ट-
मङ्गल, अस्, m. a horse with a white face, tail,
mane, breast, and hoofs; (अम्), n. a collection of
eight lucky things to be assembled on certain occa-
sions (such as a coronation &c.), e. g. a lion, a bull, an
elephant, a water-jar, a fan, a flag, a trumpet, and a
lamp; or, according to others, a Brāhman, a cow,
fire, gold, ghee, the sun, water, and a king.
—अष्ट-
मान, अम्, n. a measure, one kuḍava.
—अष्ट-
मासिक, अस्, आ, अम्, occurring once in eight months.
—अष्ट-मूर्ति, इस्, m. eight-formed, an epithet of
Śiva (as identified with the five elements, mind,
egotism, and matter; or, according to the opening of
the Śakuntalā, with the five elements, the sun and
moon and the sacrificing priest).
—अष्टमूर्ति-
धर, अस्, m. possessing eight forms, an epithet
of Śiva.
—अष्ट-रत्न, अम्, n. the eight jewels,
title of a collection of eight Ślokas on ethics.
—अष्ट-
रसाश्रय (˚स-आश्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, endowed or furnished
with the eight rasas or sentiments of poetry.
—अष्-
टर्च (˚टन्-ऋच्), अस्, m. a psalm or hymn consisting
of eight verses.
—अष्ट-लोहक, अम्, n. a class of
eight metals, gold, silver, copper, tin, lead, the magnet,
muṇḍaloha (?), and tīkṣṇaloha or steel (?).
—अष्ट-
वर्ग, अस्, m. a class of three principal medicaments
(mostly the roots of plants from the hills), named
Ṛṣabha, Jīvaka, Medā, Mahāmedā, Ṛddhi, Vṛd-
dhi, Kākolī, and Kṣīrakākolī.
—अष्ट-विध, अस्,
आ, अम्, eight-fold, of eight kinds.
—अष्ट-शत,
अम्, n. eight hundred.
—अष्ट-श्रवण, अस्, or
अष्ट-श्रवस्, आस्, m., N. of Brahmā (eight-eared,
see अष्ट-कर्ण).
—अष्टसाहस्रिक, अस्, आ, अम्,
consisting of eight thousand.
—अष्टा-कपाल, अस्,
ई, अम्, (an oblation) prepared or offered in eight pans;
(अस्), m. a sacrifice in which ghee or clarified butter
is offered in eight pans.
—अष्टाक्षर (˚टन्-अक्˚),
अस्, आ, अम्, containing eight syllables; (अस्), m., N.
of an author.
—अष्टा-गव, अम्, n. a car or wain, one
drawn by eight oxen.
—अष्टाङ्ग (˚टन्-अङ्˚), अम्,
n. eight parts of the body with which very profound
obeisance is performed (viz. the hands, breast, fore-
head, eyes, throat, and middle of the back; or the
first four, with the knees and feet; or these six, with
the speech and mind); the eight parts of a court, or
the law, the judge, assessors, scribe, and astrologer,
gold, fire, and water; any whole consisting of eight
parts or members; a die, dice; (अस्, आ, अम्), con-
sisting of eight parts or members.
—अष्टाङ्ग-
नय, अस्, m. = अष्टाङ्ग.
—अष्टाङ्ग-पात or
अष्टाङ्ग-प्रणाम, अस्, m. prostration of the eight
parts of the body as in reverence.
—अष्टाङ्ग-
हृदय, अम्, n. title of a medicinal work.
—अष्-
टाङ्गार्घ्य (˚ग-अर्˚), अस्, m. an offering of eight
articles, water, milk, kuśa grass, curds, ghee, rice,
barley, and mustard; or honey, red oleander flow-
ers, and sandal are substituted for the last three.
—अष्टा-दंष्ट्र = अष्ट-दंष्ट्र, q. v.
—अष्-
टादश-भुजा, f., N. of the wife of Śiva.
—अष्टा-
दशाङ्ग (˚शन्-अङ्˚), अस्, m. a decoction of eighteen
ingredients.
—अष्टाध्यायी (˚टन्-अध्˚), f. title of
the eleventh Kāṇḍa of the Śatapatha-Brāhmaṇa, con-
sisting of eight lectures.
—अष्टानवत, अस्, ई, अम्,
the ninety-eighth.
—अष्टा-पद, अस्, m. a spider;
a worm; a fabulous animal with eight legs, the Śa-
rabha; a wild sort of jasmin; a pin or bolt; the
mountain Kailāsa or abode of Kuvera; (अस्, अम्), m.
n. a kind of chequered cloth or board for drafts, dice,
&c.; gold.
—अष्टा-पद-पत्त्र, अम्, n. gold-leaf;
a sheet of gold.
—अष्टा-पाद्, त्, -पदी, m. f., Ved.
having eight legs, consisting of eight members; (in
[]
ritual language) a term for a pregnant animal; (पदी),
f. a wild sort of jasmin.
—अष्टा-पाद, अस्, आ, अम्,
quartered by eight, having eight for the root.
—अष्-
टा-पाद्य, अस्, आ, अम्, eight-fold.
—अष्टार-चक्र-
वत् (˚टन्-अर्˚), आन्, m. having a wheel with eight
spokes, an epithet of Mañju-śrī, a Jaina saint and
ruler.
—अष्टा-रथ, अस्, m., N. of a son of Bhīma-
ratha.
—अष्टा-वक्र, अस्, m., N. of a Brāhman, a
son of Kahoḍa.
—अष्टास्र (˚टन्-अस्˚), अम्, n. an oc-
tagon.
—अष्टास्रय (˚टन्-अस्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, octan-
gular.
—अष्टाह (˚टन्-अह्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, lasting eight
days.

अष्टक, अस्, आ, अम्, consisting of eight parts,
eight-fold; one who studies or is acquainted with the
eight books of Pāṇini's grammar or the formulas of
the Veda; (अस्), m. the eighth part, e. g. of the Ṛg-
veda; N. of a son of Viśvāmitra; (आ), f. the eighth
day after full moon; especially the eighth day of
three months, on which the progenitors or manes are
worshipped; worship of the progenitors or manes on
certain days, vegetables, flesh, and cake being seve-
rally offered upon these occasions, and the Brāhmans
feasted; (अम्), n. a whole consisting of eight parts,
e. g. the eight sections of Pāṇini's grammar.
—अष्-
टकाङ्ग (˚क-अङ्˚), अम्, n. a kind of board or cloth
for playing with dice on, having eight divisions.
आष्टक आष्टक, N. of a region.
अष्टकिन्, ई, m. one who performs an Aṣṭakā.

अष्टतय, अम्, n. a conjunction or aggregate of
eight.

अष्टातय, अस्, ई, अम्, consisting of eight parts;
(अम्), n. collection of eight things.

अष्टम, अस्, ई, अम्, the eighth; (अस्), m. the
eighth part; (ई), f. (scil. रात्रि), the eighth day
(night) in a half-month; N. of the medicinal plant
Kṣīrakākolī, the last of a class of eight medicinal
plants.
—अष्टम-कालिक, अस्, आ, अम्, one who
omitting seven meals partakes only of the eighth.
—अष्टमांश (˚म-अं˚), an eighth part.

आष्टम आष्टम, अस्, m. (fr. अष्टम), the
eighth part.
अष्टमक, अस्, आ, अम्, the eighth.
अष्टमिका, f. a śukti or weight of four tolas.

आष्टमिक, अस्, ई, अम्, taught in the eighth book
(of Pāṇini).

1. अष्टि, इस्, f., N. of a metre consisting of sixty-
four syllables.
अष्टि 2. अष्टि, इस्, f. (fr. rt. 1. अस्), Ved. reaching.
2. अष्टि; for ‘rt. 1. अस्’ read rt. 1. अश्.
3. अष्टि, इस्, f. (fr. rt. 2. अस्), seed (= अष्ठि).

अष्टिन्, ई, इनी, इ, consisting of eight members or
syllables.

अष्ट्रा अष्ट्रा, f. (fr. rt. 1. अश्?), Ved. a
prick or goad for driving cattle; (sometimes regarded
as the badge of the agriculturist, as the staff is of the
Brāhman); [cf. Zend astrâ; Lith. akstinas.].
—अष्-
ट्रा-विन्, ई, इणी, इ, Ved. obeying the goad.

आष्ट्र आष्ट्र, अम्, n. (fr. rt. 1. अश्), ether,
sky, atmosphere.

आष्ट्री आष्ट्री, f., Ved. kitchen, fire-place;
(if fr. rt. 1. अश्, according to Sāy.) an extensive forest.
